items.summary: A new non-buildable merchant tier converts a finished high-tier item into a stat-boosted version carrying match-wide random negatives, so it's a between-match variance lever rather than an edge to whoever reaches The Broker first (rolls are symmetric). Because it only activates at ~30 min and pays teams that bank and stall, it runs against this patch's earlier, more contested soul economy — the tier raises the ceiling for games that still go long, and largely idles in the tempo games the patch is pushing.
items.build_shift: It converts an existing completed slot rather than adding one, so a bad negative roll can brick a core item — expect late-game players to hold a spare high-tier slot or delay a purchase until after the first ~30-min shipment rather than buy greedily into an unknown roll.

notable_item_stories: Corrupted items are the only new late-game power layer in a patch that pulled income earlier (Bell Tower, Sunken Plaza, contested Soul Bags), so its real value is inversely tied to how fast lobbies now close.
Street Brawl's Round 5 Corrupted grant imports the tier into draft-mode mid-game, where symmetric rolls matter more than raw stats — watch whether it reshapes late Brawl picks.
No hero has Corrupted items as a core or situational build slot (it isn't a buildable item), so there is no direct core-item hero link to trace this patch.
